title: Collection of non‑cardiac sequelae after Fontan operation in childhood and adolescence.
summary:
Background
Since 1968 a special heart‑surgery method (the so‑called Fontan operation) has been used for children with severe heart malformations. In this procedure the blood from the large body veins is directed straight to the lungs, so the heart does not have to pump it actively. This change creates, among other things, a permanently elevated pressure in the large veins. Over the long term, not only the heart but also other organs such as the liver and the intestine can become impaired. The liver may develop disease, and the intestine can lose important endogenous proteins, leading to many additional problems. How often these complications occur and what their consequences are has been little studied.

Research question
The planned investigation aims to systematically determine how frequently liver disease and intestinal protein loss occur in children and adolescents who have undergone this heart operation. At the same time, the study will examine the clinical consequences of these complications and which factors increase the risk for them.

Methodology
This is a retrospective analysis of already existing patient data. All 361 patients who were treated at the University Hospital Bonn for this heart operation during the past five years will be examined. The researchers will collect demographic information, details of the surgery, laboratory values, imaging studies (e.g., liver ultrasound), and data on any symptoms and disease course. The evaluation will be completed within six months. The goal is to obtain a comprehensive picture of the incidence, severity, and possible risk factors from the existing records.
conditions: Congenital malformations of the circulatory system

interventions.name:
Retrospective analysis of all patients who were treated at our centre with a status‑post Fontan operation between 01 Nov 2020 and 01 Nov 2025.
In this retrospective single-center cohort study, data from 361 patients after Fontan surgery documented in the hospital information system will be analyzed

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who have undergone a Fontan operation and are receiving pediatric care at the Center for Pediatrics of the University Hospital Bonn.
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete documentation for the primary endpoints.
